title: 5 big analyst AI moves: Google reaffirmed as top pick after Gemini agent launch
source_used: Yahoo Finance (carrying the Investing.com article); the Investing.com page is blocked (HTTP 403)
key_facts: BMO Capital Markets reiterated an Outperform rating and Top Pick status on Alphabet after it unveiled Gemini Agent, a unified enterprise AI agent that competes with Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots.
BMO says about 80% of Google Cloud customers use Google's AI products and around 500 enterprise customers each processed over 1 trillion tokens in the past year.
BMO highlighted a 98% drop in cost per token since 2024 and said expert calls suggest token prices may bottom around 2030.
Citi named AMD, Texas Instruments, Lam Research, Teradyne and Synopsys as top Buy-rated chip picks ahead of third-quarter earnings and downgraded NXP to Neutral.
After Marvell raised its long-term revenue outlook at its analyst day, TD Cowen upgraded it to Buy and several brokers raised price targets.
Truist started coverage of IBM at Hold with a $240 target; IBM shares fell more than 20% after a second-quarter miss.
quote_evidence: BMO Capital Markets has reiterated an Outperform rating and Top Pick status on Alphabet after the company unveiled Gemini Agent, a unified enterprise AI agent, putting it in direct competition with Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots.
The analysts highlighted a 98% drop in cost per token since 2024, even as AI-related revenue has soared on rising enterprise volumes that BMO said are still in the early innings.
Alphabet "remains a clear leader across the AI stack," BMO stressed, arguing that full-stack ownership will let it benefit from optimizations at every layer as AI scales.
why_it_matters_hint: Analysts say the enterprise-agent launch eases fears that Alphabet is losing its edge in AI, but these are broker opinions.
event_date: Gemini Agent launched 8 Oct 2026; BMO note reported 9 Oct 2026
notes: Older news re-dated: our 9 Oct 2026 edition (item 52) carried the Gemini Agent launch. Text read on Yahoo Finance, which republishes the Investing.com piece (the Investing.com byline is on the page), so Investing.com stays the source and the link is its original.
